The bill would remove the duty for employers to offer a superannuation fund choice to temporary residents and when funds merge.
Employers would no longer need to give a standard choice form to temporary visa holders or when an employee’s super benefits transfer to a successor fund after a merger.
The government says employee entitlements to super contributions and their ability to choose a fund would not be affected.
Removes the obligation to offer a choice of super fund to temporary residents.
Removes the obligation to offer a choice of super fund when super funds merge.
Employers, temporary residents, and employees whose super funds merge.

The bill simplifies when employers must offer a standard choice form to employees, removing the requirement for temporary residents (including New Zealand residents) and when a superannuation fund merges, and expands eligibility for the free small business superannuation clearing house to businesses with turnover under $2 million or fewer than 20 employees, saving an estimated $45 million annually in compliance costs.
